title: Bram and the Safehouse
premise: Wren Ravensworth, a crash investigator haunted by the unexplained death of her family in row twelve, is approached by Bram Calloway, a man who claims she once saved his life — a favor she has no memory of. He belongs to a covert network that trains operatives through staged disasters like the one that killed her family, and he wants out, offering Wren the evidence to burn it from the inside. As they go on the run together, love blooms against duty while the network's hunters close in and Wren discovers her own recruitment was planned years ago. In the end, Wren exposes the network at devastating personal cost: Bram sacrifices himself to get the files public, and Wren survives to testify, carrying justice outside the law and grief in equal measure.
about_author: Vesper Ravensworth is the pen name of a former aviation safety analyst who spent a decade reading black-box transcripts before turning to fiction. They write thrillers about ordinary people trapped inside systems designed to erase them.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Twelve years after the crash that killed her family, Wren works crash investigations by day and obsesses over anomalies in the row twelve wreckage file by night. A routine inspection turns strange when she finds her own signature on a document dated before the crash. Emotional beat: the past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram Calloway appears at Wren's apartment claiming she pulled him from a burning car in 2013 — an event she cannot remember. He leaves a burner phone and a warning: they've noticed her digging. Emotional beat: uneasy debt, the sense of being watched by something patient.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. When Wren's supervisor dies in a suspicious single-car accident hours after she reports the forged signature, she calls the burner. Bram reveals the network stages disasters to train operatives — row twelve was a live exercise. Emotional beat: grief weaponized into purpose.

chapters.title: The Training Ground
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram takes Wren to an abandoned airfield where recruits are broken and rebuilt, showing her how he was made. She recognizes the instructor who signed her family's autopsy. Emotional beat: horror of understanding; the enemy has a curriculum.

chapters.title: Rules That Keep Getting Rewritten
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Using her investigator credentials, Wren pulls maintenance records linking three 'accidents' to one shell company. The network retaliates by framing her for evidence tampering. Emotional beat: the law she served now hunting her; duty inverted.

chapters.title: Safehouse
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Holed up in Bram's old network safehouse, the two strip each other's secrets bare — his kills, her survivor's guilt — and cross the line from allies to lovers. Emotional beat: tenderness as rebellion; love against duty.

chapters.title: The Handler
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram's former handler, Marek, offers him reinstatement in exchange for Wren, revealing Bram's memory of the rescue was implanted — the favor never happened. Wren overhears. Emotional beat: betrayal, and the question of what love means when built on a lie.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren chooses Bram anyway and they execute their plan: copying the network's archive during a training exercise gone live. The op half-succeeds — they get the core files but trigger a facility lockdown. Emotional beat: terror and resolve fused; no way back.

chapters.title: Time Already Running Out
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Cornered at a rail yard with hunters converging, Bram realizes only a decoy can get the files to a journalist. He takes the network's trackers onto himself and walks the other way. Emotional beat: sacrifice as the final proof of a real choice.

chapters.title: What Survives
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The files break publicly; hearings begin; Marek is arrested. Wren testifies under her own name, visits row twelve's memorial, and finds Bram alive — burned, hunted, but breathing — having faked his death with Marek's coerced help. Emotional beat: justice outside the law, survival with its price paid, and a future chosen freely.
